title: Livelihood Protests by Retirees and Workers Spread Across Iranian Cities
detail: Social Security retirees, plundered depositors, coal miners, truck drivers, bakers, and students staged protests across Tehran, Shush, Ahvaz, Dezful, Kermanshah, Rasht, Karaj, and Tabriz, defying temperatures exceeding 50°C in some cities. Demonstrators demanded pension increases in line with the cost of living, overdue payments, free healthcare, and the release of detained workers, chanting slogans including 'Enough of warmongering, our tables are empty' and 'Inflation and high prices, no to war and ruin.' The protests reflect deepening public anger over the economic toll of sanctions, currency collapse, and the resumed war with the US and Israel, coming just days after the conclusion of Ali Khamenei's state funeral.

media.caption: Retirees and workers protest economic hardship across Iranian cities

confidenceReason: Sourced from opposition-aligned outlets (NCRI/Iran Focus, both affiliated with the MEK); independent Tier 1-2 confirmation of protest scale not found. Reported patterns are consistent with prior documented economic protests.
